newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher but off earlier highs.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher but off earlier highs.

text.p: Late profit taking pressed KCBT hard red winter wheat futures to close higher but off the intraday highs achieved earlier in the session amid short covering, traders said.
KCBT wheat opened higher and gained further at the midsession as short covering lifted the front end of the market.

"The Dec continued to lead our rallies, but as we get nearer to delivery, the market has to go back to the fundamentals of the cash trade. It appeared today as if the cash market was (softening)," a KCBT trader said.
Traders said U.S. wheat values were also underpinned by signs that Turkey was closer to easing restrictions on importing U.S. wheat.

KCBT wheat closed steady to six cents per bushel higher, with Dec up six cents at $4.53-1/2. March gained 5-3/4 cent to close at $4.09-1/4. Traders said the December/March inverted spread traded late at 44 cents after having traded as wide as 48 cents. It traded late Friday at 43 cents.
Continuing in what traders said was a recent pattern of short covering, Cargill division CIS bought 900,000 Dec bushels and sold 800,000 March.
CIS also bear-spread 700,000 Dec/March at 44 to 45 cents. E D & F Man International bought two million March bushels. Refco bought 600,000 Dec and 700,000 March, traders said.
